subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Transmission Losses: Where Power Vanishes
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Transmission Losses: Where Power Vanishes.

hook.text: About 5% of all electricity generated is lost before it reaches a customer.

buildup.text: Resistance in wires converts current to heat. Longer lines lose more.

discovery.text: Corona discharge around high-voltage lines ionizes air and wastes energy as glow.

twist.text: Transformer cores lose energy to hysteresis — the iron heats up with every AC cycle.

climax.text: Reducing losses by 1% globally would save more energy than many countries use.

punchline.text: Every kilometer of wire is a tiny heater nobody wanted.

quiz.question: What causes corona discharge losses on transmission lines?
options: Rain hitting the power lines creates short circuits
High voltage ionizes the surrounding air, wasting energy as a visible glow
Wind vibration loosens the cable connections
